rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Linnaeus's sexual system was artificial: a few floral characters carried the whole classification. Bentham and Hooker built a natural system from many characters at once. A phylogenetic system tries to follow ancestry.
A taxonomic key works by paired contrasts. A herbarium sheet, a botanical garden and a flora manual are the aids that let someone else check the identification. The species remains the basic unit.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Flora vs monograph:** flora covers all plants of a region; a monograph covers all species of one taxon worldwide.  ·  **Natural vs phylogenetic:** natural groups by overall similarity (may or may not match evolution); phylogenetic groups strictly by descent.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Match the organism to the character.  ·  A product does not move an organism into another kingdom.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Bentham & Hooker's Genera Plantarum (1862–83)*** — the natural classification still cited in South Asian herbaria.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Classification systems track biology's tools:** morphology alone → all-round characters → DNA; each new data type rewrote the tree.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Hierarchy: Kingdom → Division → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species; mango = Anacardiaceae, Sapindales, Dicotyledonae.  ·  Taxonomic aids: herbarium, botanical garden, museum, key, flora, monograph, manual.  ·  Key = paired contrasting couplets leading stepwise to identification.  ·  Systems: artificial (Linnaeus — few arbitrary characters), natural (Bentham & Hooker 1862–83 — overall affinity), phylogenetic (Engler & Prantl; modern APG — molecular evolution).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: "Flora of Nepal" is the national flora project cataloguing Nepal's ~7,000 flowering plants.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Herbarium sheet label:** must carry scientific name, family, place and date of collection, collector — a specimen without data is scientifically worthless.  ·  Know one named example per system — Linnaeus, Bentham & Hooker, APG — questions expect names with dates.  ·  "An artificial key identifies; a natural system explains."
